quick: Do not breastfeed; may suppress lactation
Gynecologic exam, vaginal bleeding, LFTs, VTE signs
summary: Tamoxifen is an estrogen agonist/antagonist (SERM) used to treat estrogen receptor-positive metastatic and early breast cancer, to reduce contralateral breast cancer, to reduce invasive breast cancer after DCIS, and to reduce breast cancer incidence in high-risk women. It carries a BOXED WARNING for uterine malignancies and thromboembolic events (stroke, pulmonary embolism), including fatal cases. Usual dose is 20 mg/day (20-40 mg/day for metastatic disease). Promptly evaluate any abnormal vaginal bleeding.
indications: Treatment of estrogen receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer (adults)
Adjuvant treatment of early-stage estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer; reduction of contralateral breast cancer
Reduction of invasive breast cancer risk in women with DCIS after surgery and radiation
Reduction of breast cancer incidence in adult women at high risk

dosage.d: 20-40 mg per day; doses >20 mg/day given in divided doses (AM and PM)

dosage.n: Usually 5-10 years; >20 mg/day adds no benefit

admin: Take tablets/oral solution daily, with or without food; for doses >20 mg give in divided morning and evening doses
Verify pregnancy status before starting in women of reproductive potential and counsel on non-hormonal contraception
Report any abnormal vaginal bleeding promptly for gynecologic evaluation
Use with caution and avoid in patients needing warfarin for the risk-reduction/DCIS indications (contraindicated)
Discard oral solution within the labeled period after first opening
moa: Tamoxifen is an estrogen agonist/antagonist. It competes with estrogen for binding to the estrogen receptor, reducing estrogen-receptor-dependent growth in breast tissue (antagonist effect in breast). It has tissue-selective agonist effects elsewhere (e.g., endometrium, bone, coagulation), which underlie both benefits and risks such as endometrial proliferation and thromboembolism.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity (e.g., angioedema, serious skin reactions) to tamoxifen or any ingredient
Concomitant warfarin therapy, or history of DVT/PE, when the indication is breast-cancer risk reduction or DCIS risk reduction
monitor: Gynecologic symptoms and abnormal vaginal bleeding (uterine malignancy)
Eye symptoms (cataract, retinopathy with long use)

preg: Contraindicated - tamoxifen can cause fetal harm. Postmarketing reports include vaginal bleeding, spontaneous abortion, birth defects and fetal death; a DES-like syndrome is a theoretical long-term risk. Advise effective non-hormonal contraception and avoid conception during and shortly after therapy.
lact: Do not breastfeed during treatment; tamoxifen may also suppress lactation. Consider the importance of the drug to the mother.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is provided for renal impairment.
hepatic: Use with caution. Liver abnormalities, including cholestasis, hepatitis, and rarely fatal liver cancer/hepatic necrosis, have occurred. Perform periodic liver function testing.

major: Warfarin / anticoagulants - tamoxifen enhances anticoagulant effect (bleeding); contraindicated in the risk-reduction/DCIS settings
Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (paroxetine, fluoxetine, bupropion, quinidine) - reduce active metabolite (endoxifen) and may lower efficacy
Cytotoxic chemotherapy - increased thromboembolic risk when combined
moderate: Aromatase inhibitors - reduced anastrozole levels if combined (do not co-administer)
minor: Estrogens - may interfere with tamoxifen's action
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Limit; no major specific interaction but supports general health.
interactions.diagnostics: May raise serum calcium (especially early in bony metastatic disease), triglycerides and liver enzymes; affects coagulation parameters with warfarin.

serious: Tumor flare / hypercalcemia in bony metastatic disease
Cataracts and retinopathy with prolonged use
rare: Severe skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome, erythema multiforme)
emergency: Signs of stroke or pulmonary embolism (sudden weakness, chest pain, breathlessness)

monitoring: Regular gynecologic evaluation; promptly investigate abnormal vaginal bleeding
Symptoms/signs of venous thromboembolism and stroke
Lipids and serum calcium (early in metastatic bone disease)
Periodic eye examination with long-term use
counsel: BOXED WARNING: report any unusual vaginal bleeding, leg swelling/pain, chest pain, breathlessness or sudden weakness immediately
Use reliable NON-hormonal contraception and do not become pregnant while taking it
Hot flushes and menstrual changes are common; tell your doctor if troublesome
Tell your doctor about all medicines, especially blood thinners and certain antidepressants (paroxetine/fluoxetine)
pk: Anticancer effect develops over weeks; full clinical benefit over months/years
Plasma peak ~5 h after a 20 mg dose
Once-daily dosing; long elimination supports steady state
Store at 20-25 C; protect from light; do not freeze/refrigerate (oral solution)
pearls: BOXED WARNING: uterine malignancies and thromboembolic events (stroke, PE) - investigate abnormal vaginal bleeding promptly
Contraindicated with warfarin or prior DVT/PE in the risk-reduction and DCIS settings
CYP2D6 converts tamoxifen to active endoxifen - avoid strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (e.g., paroxetine, fluoxetine, bupropion)
Tumor flare/hypercalcemia can occur early in bony metastatic disease
Used for chemoprevention in high-risk women, not only for established cancer
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the usual schedule - do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Experience is limited. Very high doses may cause acute neurotoxicity (tremor, hyperreflexia, unsteady gait, dizziness) and QT prolongation. There is no specific antidote; treat supportively with cardiac (ECG) monitoring.
